main.derivation: Input. Chosen in DESIGN.md or with the dev-only theme picker.

on-main.derivation: White or a near-black in the main hue (L 0.17), whichever contrasts more with `main`.

on-main-muted.derivation: `on-main` blended 22% toward `main`, solved to at least 7:1 on `main`.

on-main-subtle.derivation: `on-main` blended 42% toward `main`, solved to at least 4.6:1 on `main`.

accent.derivation: Input. Chosen in DESIGN.md or with the dev-only theme picker.

on-accent.derivation: White or a near-black in the main hue (L 0.16), whichever keeps the higher contrast against both `accent` and `accent-600`.

paper.derivation: L 0.967 in the main hue, chroma a quarter of the tint.

ink.derivation: The main hue at L 0.32 (or `main`'s lightness if darker) with the full tint, solved to at least 7:1 on `paper`.

muted.derivation: The main hue at L 0.62 with 80% of the tint, solved to at least 6:1 on `paper`.

narrative.overview:
The site reads like a clean map with annotations laid over it. The content is the terrain: plain, readable, generously spaced on light paper. The work is the surveyed ground: the five projects are numbered stations on one dashed traverse that crosses the hero's topography and continues down the Projects section past each station's data sheet. On top of the terrain sit the annotations: callouts whose leader lines run from each headline to its label, a legend of symbols, dates set in the margin like coordinates, small accent squares as markers, thin hairline rings, a survey reticle around the portrait, a faint survey grid under every band and topographic contours in the dark ones. Only the annotation lines move, drawing themselves in as they come into view. The annotations orient the visitor; they never compete with the content.

Two dark bands in the main color bracket the page: the hero at the top and the contact band at the bottom, with the header pinned in the same color. Everything between alternates paper and white. The single accent color is the signal: actions, the current state, and the markers that make the map legible. Components are precise and confident: crisp radii, solid accent fills, tight labels.

The whole palette comes from two inputs, main and accent, and every text color is solved for WCAG contrast against its background, so the system holds for any pair.
keyCharacteristics: Two input colors; every other shade derived and contrast-solved.
Expanded-width Archivo headings over plain Archivo body text, with JetBrains Mono as the annotation voice.
Flat surfaces with hairline rings; depth appears only on interaction and for floating layers.
Map motifs (contours, grid, reticle, square markers, station marks) used as line art, never as fills.
Annotations behave like a map's: callouts with leader lines, a symbol legend, coordinates in the margin, and lines that draw themselves in.
The work is surveyed ground: the five projects are numbered stations on one dashed traverse that runs from the hero into their data sheets.

rules.name: The Two-Input Rule
rules.body: Only `main` and `accent` are chosen, in the frontmatter or with the dev-only theme picker's Save to DESIGN.md. Every other color is derived by `src/theme.ts` and never edited by hand; `npm run tokens` overwrites the derived keys.

rules.name: The Any-Pair Rule
rules.body: Components reference roles, never the default pair. Text on `main` uses the `on-main` family and text on `accent` uses `on-accent`, because either may flip between white and near-black. Nothing assumes `main` is dark or `accent` is orange.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: The accent marks action, current state and markers. It is never a background for large areas or a decoration for its own sake.

rules.name: The Small-Text Rule
rules.body: Small accent-colored text always uses `accent-ink` on light surfaces and `accent-glow` on main, never the raw `accent`.

rules.name: The Map Legend Rule
rules.body: Uppercase mono with wide tracking is for labels, dates and metadata only. Sentences are never set in it.

rules.name: The Lift-On-Intent Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow at rest except floating layers. Shadows answer interaction or mark something that floats above the page.

rules.name: The Square Marker Rule
rules.body: List bullets, callout markers and timeline waypoints are small accent squares. Round dots are reserved for the timeline's company stops (filled accent for the current one). Projects alone get the station mark (a ring with a triangle).

rules.name: The Survey Line Rule
rules.body: Only annotation lines move. Callout leaders, the timeline rail, its stops and its leaders draw in once, the first time they scroll into view. Content is never hidden waiting for scroll, and reduced motion shows the finished lines.

dos: **Do** change the palette by editing `colors.main` and `colors.accent` in this file and running `npm run tokens`.
**Do** style with the theme tokens (`bg-main`, `text-on-main-muted`, `text-accent-ink`, and so on) so every color follows the theme.
**Do** keep orange small text on `accent-ink` or `accent-glow` (The Small-Text Rule).
**Do** use Radix icons for every icon.
**Do** respect reduced motion: the line draw-ins, the hero load-in and the reticle rotation all switch off.
**Do** reuse a legend symbol wherever its fact appears, and add new facts to `legend` first.
donts: **Don't** hard-code hex values or Tailwind palette colors (`text-white`, `neutral-*`) in components. The exceptions are white card surfaces, black-alpha hairlines and shadows, and the status colors in the contrast grades.
**Don't** use thick colored side stripes on cards or toasts as an accent.
**Don't** set sentences in the uppercase mono label style (The Map Legend Rule).
**Don't** add shadows to surfaces at rest (The Lift-On-Intent Rule).
**Don't** put a label or kicker above a headline or card title; section names go in the callout and card categories in a corner tag.
**Don't** fade or slide content in on scroll; only lines move (The Survey Line Rule).
